articles.title: Amnesty accuses Russia of trafficking foreigners to fight in Ukraine
articles.summary: Report reveals foreign nationals were misled with job offers, then forced into Russia’s army upon arrival.
articles.body:
A new report by Amnesty International has accused Russia of tricking foreigners into fighting on Ukraine’s front lines in what amounts to “human trafficking”.

Victims from Brazil, Colombia, Sri Lanka and South Africa were duped into travelling to Russia to take up well-paid civilian or non-combat jobs, then forced to join the Russian army on arrival, according to the report released on Thursday.

Russian recruiters also targeted migrants and refugees in Russia and coerced them into joining the military, the report said.

“Amnesty’s research demonstrates how Russia’s Armed Forces are bolstering their ranks with economically vulnerable foreign nationals and using them as cannon fodder in the war of aggression against Ukraine,” said Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International’s secretary general.

“The level of exploitation and coercion involved led us to conclude that in many cases this amounts to human trafficking, as defined under the [United Nations] Palermo Protocol,” Callamard added.

Amnesty International interviewed prisoners of war at two Ukrainian camps between 2024 and 2026.

The rights group also spoke with foreign nationals currently serving with Russian forces and members of their families as well as lawyers, human rights activists and journalists.

It found local agents and misleading online job advertisements were used to deceive foreign nationals in their home countries.

A South African man who applied online for a driving job in Poland was told to fly to Moscow to pick up a truck and drive it to Poland. His wife told Amnesty International: “Upon arrival to Moscow, everything was taken from him. He was told that he would not be going to Poland and that he is becoming a soldier.”

Many recruits were promised lucrative salaries and sign-up bonuses that were not fulfilled.

All the interviewees said their freedom of movement was severely restricted after signing military contracts.

During training, recruits from Brazil and Sri Lanka said their passports and mobile phones were taken from them before being sent to the front line.

Both Russia and Ukraine have recruited thousands of foreign nationals into their armies since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine four-and-a-half years ago.

Amnesty says it cannot conduct inquiries about foreigners in Ukraine’s army as it has no access to prisoners of war held in Russia, which designates Amnesty as a “foreign agent”.

An estimated 28,000 foreigners from 136 countries are said to be fighting in the Russian army and officials believe Russia deployed some 14,000 North Korean troops to battle Ukraine’s 2024 incursion into the Kursk region.

Meanwhile, Ukraine says 16,000 foreign nationals from more than 70 countries – including nearly 40 percent from Latin America – are currently serving in the Ukrainian army.

Russia has previously dismissed accusations of coercing foreigners into joining its army.

articles.title: Iran-backed terror group’s latest territorial grab threatens second global shipping chokepoint
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces seized Yemen's Mocha port and advanced toward Bab el-Mandeb, threatening Red Sea shipping as Brent crude surged past $106.
articles.body: Iran-backed Houthi forces seized Yemen’s strategic port city of Mocha on Thursday and pushed toward positions overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, opening a potentially dangerous new front for global trade as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely constrained. The advance threatens the southern gateway to the Red Sea just as Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on that route to bypass Hormuz — putting pressure on critical shipping lanes on both sides of the Arabian Peninsula and raising the risk of further disruptions to oil and commercial traffic through a key global trade choke point. "Now you have Iran on one side of the Arabian Peninsula controlling Hormuz, and now the Houthis controlling Bab el-Mandeb on the other side of the peninsula," Hisham Al-Omeisy, senior Yemen advisor at the European Institute of Peace, told Fox News Digital. "Which basically is going to drive prices — oil prices, goods and everything else — up exponentially." IRAN-BACKED TERROR PROXY HOUTHIS THREATEN FRESH ATTACKS AFTER YEMEN AIRPORT STRIKE On background, a senior administration official told Fox News Digital: "The United States is focused on protecting our core national security interests — such as ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea — while empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges. We are in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen Government regarding regional stability." Yemeni government sources said Thursay the Houthis captured Mocha and reached the Hanish Islands, while Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces withdrew south toward Dhubab, which sits directly on the Bab el-Mandeb opposite the strategic island of Perim. Control of Dhubab and Perim would be critical to gaining a stronger hold over the strait, Yemeni government sources told Reuters on Sept. 10. Bab el-Mandeb is only about 18 miles wide at its narrowest point and connects the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea and, farther north, the Suez Canal. It is a major artery for goods moving between Asia and Europe as well as energy shipments. Its importance has grown dramatically during the Iran conflict. WHO CONTROLS THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ RIGHT NOW? HERE'S WHAT THE SHIP TRAFFIC ACTUALLY SHOWS The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported Sept. 9 that crude oil and petroleum liquids moving through Bab el-Mandeb averaged 8.1 million barrels per day in the second quarter of 2026, up from 5.4 million barrels per day in the final quarter of 2025. At the same time, flows through Hormuz plunged from 21.6 million barrels per day to just 4.9 million. The EIA attributed the increase at Bab el-Mandeb in part to Saudi Arabia rerouting crude through its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to avoid Hormuz. Al-Omeisy said the danger extends beyond the Houthis’ geographical gains. He said retreating government forces left behind military materiel that could strengthen Houthi forces on other fronts. "People are focused on taking Mocha and those outposts on the Red Sea," Al-Omeisy said. "But the military side is terrible, particularly the equipment, the munitions, the vehicles, the drones that were at those military camps, which they can now, in turn, use against the government forces elsewhere." RUBIO ACCU.S.ES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES Reuters separately reported Thursday that Iranian arms and direct guidance from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards helped the Houthi advance, citing Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources. Two Iranian sources told Reuters that Tehran had instructed the Houthis to intensify attacks on Saudi Arabia and promised additional funding, weapons and senior officers. Iran has publicly denied directing Houthi operations. The seizure comes amid what conflict-monitoring organization ACLED described Sept. 9 as the most serious escalation between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed camp since hostilities resumed in mid-July. ACLED recorded at least 276 fatalities between Sept. 3 and 7 as clashes spread across al-Dali, al-Bayda, Marib, Shabwa, al-Jawf, al-Hudayda and Taizz, according to an analysis published Sept. 9. Sherwan Hindreen Ali, ACLED’s Middle East research manager, said fighting along the Red Sea coast had become particularly intense as both sides sought control over territory with direct strategic importance to Bab el-Mandeb. "Fighting will remain focused on the fronts of the Red Sea coast in al-Hudaydah and Taizz, where both the Houthis and the Saudi Arabia/IRG have a vested interest in claiming the whole territory to deprive the other side of effective control of the strait of Bab el-Mandab," Ali said in an analysis. Saudi Arabia itself has also become more deeply involved. EXPERT WARNS OF 'GENERAL ESCALATION' OF FIGHTING IF HOUTHIS RESUME RED SEA CAMPAIGN Ali said Saudi forces launched at least 15 strikes against the Houthis between Sept. 3 and 7, mostly around Taizz, marking the highest number of Saudi strikes since Riyadh resumed military engagement against the Houthis in July. The Houthis responded Sept. 8 with what Ali described as their largest wave of direct attacks on Saudi territory since March 2022, launching dozens of drones and ballistic missiles toward Abha, Jizan, Najran and Khamis Mushait. Ali said the attacks injured 73 people. The widening fighting is now posing an early test for a new joint defense agreement between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. Al-Omeisy said the international response allowed the Houthis to exploit divisions among their opponents. "The Houthis are also good in exploiting divisions and delays, they move rapidly on the ground to force a status quo while the international community debates merits, responsibilities and costs of an intervention." The escalation also raises questions about Saudi Arabia’s newly signed defense agreement with Pakistan and Turkey. IRAN-BACKED HOUTHI THREAT IN RED SEA COULD LEAD TO MAJOR US POLICY SHIFT, ANALYSTS SAY The agreement, signed last month in Mecca, states that an armed attack against one member will be considered an attack against all three, Reuters reported Sept. 10. But after Houthi drones and ballistic missiles struck Saudi cities and energy infrastructure this week, Pakistan said Thursday that no military response under the pact was currently being discussed. "There is no such thing under discussion right now," Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said, according to Reuters. "When time comes [we] will act under the agreement." The Houthis, meanwhile, have said international navigation through the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb remains safe, while maintaining that Saudi vessels are subject to their previously announced blockade, Reuters reported Thursday. Al-Omeisy warned that reversing the Houthis’ latest territorial gains could become increasingly difficult. "The Houthis are really good at capturing a position, they entrench really well," he said. "They send these massive reinforcements, and then it’s going to be extremely difficult to push them out of those areas." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Oil markets were already responding to the widening regional threat Thursday. Brent crude jumped more than 5% to $106.60 a barrel by late Thursday morning, while U.S. crude climbed above $100 for the first time since May, according to Reuters. Reuters contributed to the story.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt tells staff to file annual asset declarations online by October
articles.summary: India News: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has made it mandatory for all govt employees, barring All India Service officers, to submit their annual statements of assets.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has made it mandatory for all govt employees, barring All India Service officers, to submit their annual statements of assets and liabilities online through the Integrated Financial and Human Resources Management System (IFHRMS).The move follows an amendment to Rule 7(3) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Conduct Rules made in Jan 2026 by the DMK regime. Employees are required to declare their immovable properties, including land and buildings, movable assets such as vehicles, jewellery and bank deposits, as well as debts and other liabilities through the IFHRMS portal. “The facility for filing details of assets and liabilities has now been enabled on the IFHRMS portal. The system will make it easier to monitor violations,,” a senior official said.In a recent communication, the govt directed secretaries, heads of departments, district collectors, judges, TNPSC secretary and registrar of Madras high court to instruct employees to file statements for the calendar year ending Dec 31, 2025, by Oct 31, 2026.The date of filing will be recorded in an employee’s ‘annual confidential report’. Failure to submit the statement within the stipulated period will be treated as a violation of the service conduct rules.Employees must file statements of their assets and liabilities as on Dec 31 of each year by March 31 of the succeeding year. The govt has also advised employees to keep their IFHRMS user IDs and passwords secure. Employees have to use Form I for immovable property, Form II for movable property and Form III for debts and other liabilities. After verifying and correcting the details, they must confirm and submit the declaration and download a copy for their records.“Not many employees take the declaration seriously. Submission of the statement will be considered during panel preparation for promotion. Making it mandatory is a welcome step as it would help prevent corruption at all levels,” said a member of Jactto-Geo, an umbrella federation of govt employees.In July, the TVK govt introduced a WhatsApp number — 9498180936 — for reporting instances of govt employees demanding bribes. articles.title: Meet Daniel Zhang, the 17-year-old San Diego student who lost his grandmother to cancer at nine, then built a 72-card cancer game reaching 1,500 children
articles.summary: US News: When Daniel Zhang was nine, cancer was something he could not understand. His grandmother had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, and the months th.
articles.body: When Daniel Zhang was nine, cancer was something he could not understand. His grandmother had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, and the months that followed were filled with hospital visits, treatments and questions that were difficult for a child to process. Years later, that experience would inspire the San Diego teenager to create something designed to help other children make sense of the disease. Now 17, Zhang is a cancer biology and bioinformatics researcher, educator and co-founder of Tumor Tactics, a 72-card educational game that turns cancer biology and treatment decisions into a strategy game for young learners. His story was recently featured by Young Planet Leaders, which named him its September 2026 Young Planet Leader.From a painful childhood experience to a game about cancerZhang’s connection with cancer began when his grandmother was diagnosed with stage 3 pancreatic cancer. According to the story behind Tumor Tactics, he spent months watching her undergo treatment and struggling to understand why medicines intended to help her could also leave her exhausted and unwell. The experience stayed with him.Years later, when cancer affected his family again, Zhang found himself trying to explain the disease to his younger sister. That experience reinforced something he had felt as a child: medical terminology could be overwhelming, particularly for young people watching someone they love go through cancer. The idea for Tumor Tactics grew from that gap.Created with fellow student Zachary Tou, the game places players in the role of doctors and asks them to make decisions based on cancer biology, treatment options and potential side effects. The creators say the aim is not to make cancer seem simple, but to make its underlying science easier for children to understand.A classroom idea that has grown beyond the cardsTumor Tactics has already attracted recognition and funding. Young Planet Leaders reports that the project has received more than $3,600 in grants, became a finalist in the ECGBL International Educational Games Competition and is scheduled to be presented at the 2026 United Nations Science Summit in New York. The game is part of a broader effort by Zhang to make science education accessible to children.He is also a co-founder and National President of STEAMLabs International, a student-led nonprofit that runs free STEM and arts programmes for young people. The organisation has reached more than 1,500 K-8 students across multiple US cities and states as well as Nigeria, according to Young Planet Leaders. California State Senator Catherine Blakespear’s office also recognised Zhang in 2025 for his work with STEAMLabs, citing more than 25 educational events reaching over 1,500 students.From cancer research to Carnegie HallZhang’s interests extend well beyond education. He conducts cancer-related research and has worked with the UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center. He was also selected for the 2026 Summer Science Program at Purdue University, according to Young Planet Leaders.At the same time, he has pursued music seriously. An all-state classical pianist, Zhang has performed at Carnegie Hall and international venues, while also helping lead HANG, a network that brings live music performances to senior-care communities in San Diego.For Zhang, however, the different strands of his work appear to meet at the same point: making complicated subjects more accessible and using what he has learned to help others. What began with a nine-year-old trying to understand his grandmother’s illness has now become a project designed to ensure that another child facing cancer does not have to feel quite as lost.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: The Department of Homeland Security removed the controversial post vilifying Sikh truck drivers but said that the criticisms were nonsensical drivel. New York Post cited a statement by the DHS amid the major row in which the department said that Mr Singh, the bearded man in the poster, was actually Harjinder Singh who caused a fatal crash killing three people because of his wrong turn on Florida's turnpike.“Harjinder Singh is an illegal alien from India who should never have been in our country,” the statement said as reported by NYT. But the department, the NYT report said, did not give any explanation as to why it had removed the post.The controversial post showed a bearded man with a bandana facing off with Optimus Prime, a character from the Transformers franchise, depicted with the seal of the Department of Homeland Security on his armor. "Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr Singh," the accompanying text said, triggering massive backlash from the Sikh American community. Singh is a common surname in India and among the Sikhs."The timing of the posting, around the anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks, drew particular criticism. After the 2001 attacks, Sikh men, who traditionally wear beards and turbans, were mistakenly targeted in numerous anti-Muslim violent incidents," the NYT report said.Hasbro says their permission was not taken“Hasbro is aware of the recent posts using our characters,” the company said in a statement. “These posts were done without permission and do not represent the Transformers brand or Hasbro.”California Governor Gavin Newsom called the post 'disgusting' before it was deleted. "Trump’s government is trafficking in racist propaganda targeting the Sikh community," Newsom wrote."Hey Gavin, YOU gave him his CDL and then he killed three people with his tractor-trailer," the department hit back.Who is Harjinder Singh?On August 12, 2025, Harjinder Singh was driving a tractor-trailer on Florida’s Turnpike near Fort Pierce/St. Lucie County. He allegedly made an unauthorized U-turn through a section marked “Official Use Only.” The truck ended up blocking traffic, and a minivan crashed into it. Three people in the minivan were killed. The US authorities said Singh had crossed the US-Mexico border illegally in September 2018. He subsequently lived in California and got his license in Washington and then in California. He was charged with three counts of vehicular homicide, along with immigration-related violations. He was initially held without bond. articles.title: After countless hours searching for rare seahorses in French Polynesia, a photographer captured an adult male beside two newborn juveniles; the image won Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A photograph showing an adult male seahorse with two tiny newborn juveniles in the shallow waters of Mo’orea, French Polynesia, has won the grand priz.
articles.body: A photograph showing an adult male seahorse with two tiny newborn juveniles in the shallow waters of Mo’orea, French Polynesia, has won the grand prize at the Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026 awards. French underwater photographer Julien Anton spent countless hours searching through underwater seaweed beds with local naturalists before finding the trio. He took the photograph during a rebreather dive using specialised lighting in the Pacific waters. The image first won the Wildlife category before being selected for the overall prize, competition organisers Oceanographic Magazine and watchmaker Blancpain announced on Thursday. More than 15,000 entries from photographers around the world were submitted across categories including Wildlife, Fine Art, Conservation and Ocean Unseen.A quiet moment after birthSeahorses are becoming increasingly rare across French Polynesia, making sightings difficult and unpredictable. In the winning photograph, the two tiny juveniles appear to turn back towards the adult male against the dark water. Male seahorses carry eggs in a special pouch and give birth to live young. This makes the scene look like a father releasing his young into the open ocean. Speaking about the award, Anton described the effort involved in finding the animals. "Winning Ocean Photographer of the Year is an immense honour – one I'm proud to share with my family, and with the local residents, naturalists and fishermen of Tahiti and Moorea whose knowledge made this image possible," Anton said in a statement published on the competition platform. "We spent countless hours searching in difficult conditions, with no guarantee of finding a single seahorse. That is what made the moment so extraordinary – when the juveniles turned back towards the adult, it felt like something far beyond what I had dared to hope for."Impact on the judging panelThe photograph's composition received strong praise from the competition judges when they reviewed the entries. Will Harrison, founder and director of the Ocean Photographer of the Year, described the panel's reaction when Anton's photograph appeared before them. "When Julien Anton's image first appeared on screen, the judging panel fell silent," Harrison stated in the award announcement. "It is an image that demands reflection, pause for thought, and it certainly got that from us. The image is full of quiet energy, even if some of that comes from us humans imprinting our own emotions on the photograph: the bow of the father's head, the juveniles turning back towards him, the generational gap and the unknown futures of the newborns. What kind of ocean are we leaving for those who come after us?"Broad field of international winnersAlong with Anton's overall prize, several other photographers won major category awards in the 2026 competition. British photographer Jenny Stock received the Female Fifty Fathoms Award, which celebrates inspiring women in ocean photography. "To be nominated by fellow ocean photographers means more to me than I can easily express – this community is everything," Stock said after receiving the award.Other category winners included:Ocean Unseen: Japanese photographer Mitsuna Kawai won the new category with a blackwater photograph showing a ribbonfish off the coast of Japan.Fine Art: Australian photographer Matty Smith won for a black-and-white image of a nurse shark surrounded by remoras swimming in formation.Adventure: Sydney-based photographer Gergo Rugli won with a photograph of wild dolphins riding a wave alongside surfers at Tamarama Beach in Sydney.Portfolio: Spanish photographer Miguel Serrano Ruiz won for a month-long documentary series showing olive ridley sea turtle conservation work in Baja California Sur, Mexico.All winning and shortlisted photographs will go on public display at the Australian National Maritime Museum in Sydney from November 19 as part of the competition's global tour.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Days after Lindsay Clancy mistrial, another Massachusetts mom accused of killing her children seeks freedom
articles.summary: Janette MacAusland's defense sought dismissal after prosecutors said they are still waiting on the medical examiner's findings in the Wellesley murder case.
articles.body: If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255). Less than a week after the closely watched Lindsay Clancy murder trial ended in a mistrial, another Massachusetts case involving a mother accused of killing her children returned to court Thursday. And the defense sought to have charges dismissed after prosecutors said they were still awaiting a medical examiner's findings. Prosecutors told the court they are still awaiting the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner's official determination of the children's cause and manner of death, prompting defense attorney Joseph Krowski to ask that the case be dismissed or that Janette MacAusland be released on bail, WCVB reported. A judge denied both requests, ordering MacAusland to remain held without bail. articles.title: Algeria cuts diplomatic ties with UAE: What we know
articles.summary: Algiers ends relations with Gulf state over ‘provocative and hostile’ actions, after years of tensions.
articles.body:
Algeria has severed diplomatic ties with the United Arab Emirates after tensions between the two countries boiled over.

Algiers on Thursday accused Abu Dhabi of a series of “provocative and hostile” actions, adding that it had exhausted attempts to preserve relations.

In an apparent response, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said diplomatic relations should be based on “rationality” rather than “riddles”.

The rupture in relations comes amid differences between the two states over Israel, Western Sahara and alleged UAE influence in North Africa and the Sahel.

Moreover, Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has repeatedly accused the UAE of interfering in Algerian and regional affairs.

“Algeria has decided to cut diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, following the exhaustion of all means to preserve bilateral relations,” state television announced.

Algeria’s Foreign Ministry accused the UAE of “provocative and hostile acts”, without providing details.

“Algeria spared no effort to draw the Emirati side’s attention to, and to warn it against, the dire consequences that could result from its regrettable and unjustified conduct,” the ministry said.

UAE Ambassador Yousef Saif Khamis Subaa Al-Ali was summoned, informed of the decision to cut diplomatic ties and given 48 hours to comply. Algeria also announced that it had decided to close its airspace to all UAE-registered aircraft starting Friday, with the exception of UAE commercial flights to and from Algiers, which are exempt until the end of the year.

Algeria had already signalled its frustration with the UAE in February when it began the process of cancelling a 2013 air services agreement between the two countries.

Shortly after Algeria announced the decision to sever ties, Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, wrote on social media that diplomatic relations should be based on “rationality, communication and clarity of interests” rather than “riddles and signals that require decoding”.

Gargash did not explicitly mention Algeria or directly link his comments to Algiers’ announcement.

“For ambiguity is not a policy, and noise does not compensate for the absence of vision; successful diplomacy is built on clarity of positions, sound management of interests and differences,” he added. “And anything beyond that is merely an expression of a deficiency in vision and management.”

The UAE Foreign Ministry said it hoped the decision would be “temporary”, saying it “affirms the UAE’s appreciation for the brotherly Algerian people and its pride in the bonds that unite the two peoples, particularly through the Algerian community ‌residing in the UAE and Algerian visitors”.

What has the Algerian president said about the UAE in the past?

Tebboune has rarely directly criticised the UAE by name, but observers say that his critical statements have clearly been directed at the Gulf state.

He has referred in speeches to a “micro-state” or “statelet” that he said was seeking to destabilise countries including Libya, Mali and Sudan, where the UAE has been accused of involvement in conflicts. The UAE has denied the allegations.

In a televised interview in July, Tebboune said the unnamed state had a “very negative impact” in the region, adding that “wherever they set foot, blood flows”.

“We want them to stay away, so that blood does not flow in our country,” he added.

At the time, Tebboune said Algeria could have broken diplomatic relations with the state much earlier but had refrained because it did not want to deepen regional divisions.

What are the differences between the UAE and Algeria’s regional positions?

Algeria opposes normalisation with Israel, while the UAE established diplomatic relations with Israel through the US-brokered Abraham Accords in 2020 and has since developed economic, diplomatic and defence ties with Israel.

Another fundamental disagreement is their position on Western Sahara. The UAE backs Morocco’s claim over the disputed territory, while Algeria supports the Polisario Front’s efforts to establish an independent Western Sahara.

The tensions with Algeria are not the UAE’s only recent regional tussle.

In January, Somalia cancelled all agreements with the UAE covering areas including ports, security and defence, accusing Abu Dhabi of actions undermining Somalia’s sovereignty, national unity and political independence. The tensions were linked in part to the UAE’s extensive ties with the breakaway region of Somaliland.

Sudan has meanwhile repeatedly accused the UAE of supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in its civil war, an allegation Abu Dhabi denies. In May, Sudan also accused the UAE of supplying drones it said were used in attacks launched from Ethiopia.

Relations between the UAE and Saudi Arabia have also become strained. Tensions have escalated in Yemen, where Saudi forces in December struck what Riyadh described as a UAE-linked weapons shipment to the separatist Southern Transitional Council, while Saudi Arabia backed demands for Emirati forces to leave Yemen.

articles.title: TSA brings back visitor gate access for some Americans
articles.summary: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is reversing policies put in place after 9/11.
articles.body:
American airports dramatically changed in the wake of 9/11, but new policy changes are restoring some previously banned travel practices after 25 years.

The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) announced that it will soon allow individuals without tickets to pass through security and go to airport gates with loved ones.

TSA is also considering allowing some US passengers to take full water bottles through security, reversing a policy that was implemented after a foiled 2006 terror plot.

The changes represent some of the biggest shifts in aviation security in decades and likely stem from improved technology rather than a decline in standards, an aviation expert told the BBC.

Americans who participate in TSA PreCheck or have a known traveller number will be the first to take advantage of the new policies. Those travellers already go through a pre-approval process with the US government in order to receive speedier security screening at US airports.

Individuals who have TSA PreCheck and want to go to an airport gate without a ticket can apply online one to three days before their planned visits.

TSA announced this week that the Gateside TSA PreCheck programme will be offered at 13 airports across the US.

"This new program makes it easier to return to the gate for welcomes and send-offs, meet friends during a layover, and enjoy dining and shopping along the way, bringing back the moments that once defined air travel," TSA wrote on its website.

Jeff Price, an aviation security expert and professor at Metro State University Denver, told the BBC that the post-9/11 policy change was about reducing the number of people security officers had to screen.

"It keeps the lines moving and allows us to focus more on the traveling passenger," he said.

But now improvements in technology mean these policies can change, he said.

In addition to reinstating gate visitors, the Trump administration is also looking at allowing passengers with TSA PreCheck to take water with them through airport security, according to US media reports.

That would reverse a ban put in place following attempted terrorist attacks in the UK in 2006, in which individuals planned to smuggle liquid chemical mixtures inside soft drink and sports drink bottles.

The BBC requested confirmation of this reported change; TSA did not respond.

Price said newer security machines that TSA is installing to replace traditional X-ray machines have computed tomography capabilities, which "can do a much better job of detecting liquid-based explosives".

These updates to security protocols follow a move from TSA last year to end the requirement that passengers remove their shoes during security screenings, an unpopular policy in place for two decades.

Reaction to the announcements on social media was mixed. Some older users who remember a time before these policies praised a return to normalcy, while younger users questioned whether the changes signaled any decline in safety.

"People have a nostalgia for a pre 9/11, it's a calling back to a normal world, and I can see that part of it," Price said. "I can see people wanting to get back to something that they feel more comfortable with, which was a pre 9/11 world."

But Price said these changes will not impact the safety of passengers as long as core security measures remain in place and standards continue to be high.

"I don't want to compromise [valid security measures] simply for a nostalgic feeling before 9/11," he said. "I don't think we should make those types of decisions so that we feel better. We can make those types of decisions as long as the security measures are not compromised, and that's always what I look for in these situations."

articles.title: Family of 9/11 hero to retrace his steps in final Tunnel to Towers stop
articles.summary: Frank Siller and family will retrace Stephen Siller's iconic run through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel to the Twin Towers on the 25th anniversary.
articles.body: The family of 9/11 hero Stephen Siller will mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks by retracing the FDNY firefighter's steps as he ran through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel toward the World Trade Center. Frank Siller and other members of the Siller family will participate in the private walk before joining hundreds of friends and supporters at the FDNY Ten House. The event will conclude the Tunnel to Towers "Steel Across America" tour, which has traveled since May bringing Siller's story and a 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower all across the nation. FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' -- THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE On the morning of 9/11, Siller had just concluded his shift with the fire department when he received word that a plane had struck the World Trade Center. "Stephen drove his truck to the entrance of the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel, but it had already been closed for security purposes. Determined to carry out his duty, he strapped 60 lbs. of gear to his back, and raced on foot through the tunnel to the Twin Towers, where he gave up his life while saving others," the tour's website recounts. NEW YORK JETS OWNER WOODY JOHNSON TO BE HONORED AT TUNNEL TO TOWERS GALA FOR DECADE-LONG PARTNERSHIP Since its founding, inspired by Siller and his favorite quote, "While we have time, let us do good," Tunnel to Towers has provided more than 1,700 mortgage-free homes to the families of fallen service members and first responders, as well as to disabled veterans and first responders. The organization has also delivered housing assistance and support services to more than 20,000 homeless veterans and holds hundreds of events nationwide to honor America’s heroes and preserve the memory of those who lost their lives for future generations. The Tunnel to Towers 9/11 Institute has helped to educate students from kindergarten through 12th grade on the "extraordinary heroism and goodness of everyday people" on Sept. 11, "while demonstrating the strength and resilience of America’s spirit." Its mobile 9/11 exhibit has traveled to nearly all 50 states as well as Canada. According to the group, this initiative will deliver 343 mortgage-free homes to the families of fallen service members and fallen first responders as well as to catastrophically injured service members across the country. Fox News' Peter Pinedo contributed to this report.

articles.title: 8.5 hours of sleep, 3 hours of reading, 15-minute afternoon nap: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby shares his daily routine
articles.summary: US News: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby starts his day before most people have even begun checking their emails, but he doesn't immediately dive into a packed.
articles.body: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby starts his day before most people have even begun checking their emails, but he doesn't immediately dive into a packed schedule of meetings. 59-year-old Kirby, who runs one of the world's biggest airlines, says he typically gets about eight and a half hours of sleep before waking at 5:30 am. His first task is not a long list of emails. He spends just about five minutes catching up on messages before turning to newspapers.He reads the Wall Street Journal cover to cover, followed by about 15 minutes of the New York Times. He then moves on to his morning workout, according to his recent podcast interview with Semafor.Kirby's approach to his workday is equally unusual.The United Airlines chief puts a strict four-hour limit on meetings each day, and he often spends less time in meetings than that. He believes meetings should be used for actual conversations rather than presentations.His preference is for executives to send slide decks in advance so that he does not have to sit through someone reading a presentation to him. That leaves Kirby with substantial time for what he considers a more important part of his job: reading, thinking and talking to people.By the end of an average day, he says he has spent around three hours reading. His reading isn't restricted to business and aviation. He also reads science fiction novels. And despite running a company with hundreds of thousands of employees and a vast global operation, Kirby sometimes makes time for something that might seem surprising for a CEO with such a demanding job: an afternoon nap.He regularly takes a 15-minute nap during the day.Kirby has said he sees his role less as managing everything that happened the previous day and more as looking ahead at what could be coming next. His routine is therefore built around giving himself enough time away from meetings and day-to-day firefighting to think about the airline's future.Kirby says he wants flight attendants to stop saying sorryThat philosophy also feeds into his vision for United's customer service. Kirby says he wants to build an airline that its employees, particularly flight attendants, are proud to work for. His goal, he says, is ultimately to “eliminate the need for them to apologize for anything.”His argument is that flight attendants should not constantly have to apologise to passengers for problems such as poor Wi-Fi, broken seats or delays that are within the airline's control.Kirby has identified four areas that he believes are essential to creating a premium airline: product, reliability, technology and service. But he considers service the most important because it determines how employees treat customers and how passengers feel about the airline.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 15-year-old boy survives days at sea after boat capsizes off Alaska, killing 2 others
articles.summary: A 15-year-old boy survived days at sea after a fishing boat capsized off Alaska, killing his older brother and cousin.
articles.body: A 15-year-old boy survived days at sea after a fishing boat capsized off Alaska, killing his older brother and cousin. The teen was rescued Monday after he was found clinging to the overturned vessel about four miles east of St. Lawrence Island, the United States Coast Guard said in a news release. Two other people were found unresponsive in the water. NBC affiliate KTUU of Anchorage identified them as the teen’s older brother and cousin. Video obtained by KTUU showed the moment the teen was rescued. The boy, appearing to wear a black hoodie underneath a coat with green pants and black boots, is seen kneeling on the vessel. The brother died after getting stuck under the boat, the 15-year-old’s mother told the news station. The cousin survived for a day but died, the woman said. The group was on an 18-foot fishing vessel near the island when it capsized. The Coast Guard said it was notified Sunday night of the overdue vessel. The boat had last been seen Friday departing Savoonga. Due to the weather and poor visibility Sunday night, an aircrew launched Monday morning to begin the search. The teen was located around 3 p.m. Monday. “Watchstanders at the Coast Guard Arctic District command center coordinated the rescue of the survivor with the Northwest Explorer, a nearby good Samaritan vessel,” the Coast Guard said. “Before departing the scene to refuel, the HC-130 aircrew deployed a line of flares to guide the Northwest Explorer to the overturned vessel.” Adam White, captain of the vessel that found the teenager, told NBC News that his crew were returning back from a NOAA survey when they received a message from the Coast Guard. After receiving coordinates for a survivor, White altered their course to look for the boy and prepared supplies to keep him warm. The seven scientists and six crew members on board all kept their eyes on the water to see if they could find him. “When he finally came into view, it was elation from everybody,” White said. “Everybody cheered.” The teenager was unable to get to the rafts near him, stuck on the top of the overturned boat about 8 miles from his last known position, White said. The crew blasted their horn “to give him some hope” that help was on its way. “We were lucky enough because the kid was so tough, so strong that that he was able to grab a hold of a heaving line that we threw to him,” White said. “And he was able to hold on while we sort of reeled him in. And I just, like, can’t believe how tough this kid is.” White says the boy was “moderately” hypothermic once they were able to get him on board. They were able to raise his body temperature until they could get him medical attention. The captain was able to meet the boy’s family, which White described as overwhelming. “We gave each other a really long hug, and they just, they had a lot of joy,” White said. “Obviously, there’s a lot of pain in their eyes — there’s a lot of sorrow. It’s just so much, so much mixed emotions.” Rear Adm. Bob Little, the commander of the Coast Guard Arctic District command center, said their hearts go out to the families and friends, and communities affected by the tragedy. “We are grateful for the incredible efforts of the motor vessel Northwest Explorer, Federal, State, Village first responders and mission partners who assisted in the effort that resulted in a life saved,” Little said.

articles.title: Man jailed after threatening to kill son's teacher in French village
articles.summary: The father had threatened to behead a female primary school teacher near Toulouse.
articles.body:
A man has been given a six-month jail term in France after he threatened to kill a female primary school teacher who had disciplined his son at a village primary school.

He was sentenced after a fast-track hearing on Thursday, six days after the events unfolded in Le Fauga, a village with a population of about 2,600 just outside the southwestern city of Toulouse.

The teacher has been granted official protection and has gone on sick leave.

French Education Minister Edouard Geffray said: "No teacher should be afraid to do their job. Attacking one of them is attacking the entire institution."

Over the summer, Geffray steered through a law aimed at protecting staff from a "significant risk" to their safety or health from a member of a student's family.

The minister said this case would trigger one of the first uses of the decree.

The case revives terrible memories in France of the beheading of a teacher in the Paris suburb of Conflans-Sainte-Honorine six years ago. Samuel Paty was murdered outside his school by an 18-year-old Chechen refugee.

In Le Fauga, the teacher's colleagues did not go into work on Monday because of what had happened the previous Friday.

The threat was made after the man had been called in for a chat with the school, according to Toulouse education chief Karim Benmiloud.

Le Fauga Mayor Jean-Marie Puig told BFMTV that the man's son had been disruptive in class and the teacher had sent him to another class to calm down, although he continued to misbehave.

The teacher in this class was alleged to have told the child to "stop acting like a little bully", BFMTV reports.

She was then threatened by the father, who according to the mayor had waited for her "outside the school and apparently threatened to cut off her head if she'd been a man".

The parent subsequently apologised, however a judicial complaint was made and he went before the prosecutor in Toulouse on Thursday afternoon.

The decree passed in July allows for a student to be transferred to another school in a case involving significant risk to staff, and where education authorities have intervened.

It is thought the boy and a younger sister may now be moved to another school outside Le Fauga.

articles.title: Israel says it has destroyed underground Hezbollah base in Lebanon
articles.summary: The Israeli military has destroyed underground positions belonging to the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militia in southern Lebanon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netan...
articles.body:
Israeli military destroys underground Hezbollah base in southern Lebanon, eliminating terrorist infrastructure and preventing hostile forces from returning.

Operation in Ali al-Taher ridge uncovers Iranian-made rockets, missiles, drones, machine guns, anti-tank missiles, mines, and explosive devices in underground facilities.

Strategic importance of the ridge in southern Lebanon highlighted by its contested nature in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah, with Israeli military continuing to operate in the security zone.

The Israeli military has destroyed underground positions belonging to the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militia in southern Lebanon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced on Thursday.

The operation completes "the consolidation of the security zone in southern Lebanon," the ministers wrote in a joint statement on X. There was initially no confirmation from the Lebanese side.

A week ago, the military took control of the Ali al-Taher ridge, both above and below ground. According to Israeli media reports, Hezbollah fighters had been entrenched there for weeks, and the area had been the scene of repeated clashes.

The Israeli military said on Telegram that the military had destroyed the underground infrastructure in the area of the strategically important ridge, following extensive preparations.

It said Hezbollah's ability to use that infrastructure to plan and carry out terrorist attacks against Israeli civilians and soldiers had been permanently eliminated.

The mayor of the nearby town of Nabatieh, Abbas al-Din, said there had been an extremely powerful explosion near the ridge. The tremors had been felt throughout southern Lebanon and even in Beirut, some 70 kilometres away. Residents reportedly said it felt like a minor earthquake.

Netanyahu and Katz said the site was "strategic terror infrastructure" that had been built over two decades with Iranian funding. Soldiers would remain there to prevent hostile forces from returning, they said.

According to the Israeli army, the now-destroyed infrastructure extended over more than two kilometres. Inside the underground facilities, dozens of Iranian-made rockets, missiles and drones had been found, along with machine guns, anti-tank missiles and hundreds of mines and explosive devices.

The military said a command centre had been located within the underground infrastructure. The complex included weapons depots and living quarters that had allowed terrorists to remain underground for extended periods. The claims cannot be independently verified.

The Ali al-Taher ridge near Nabatieh is considered strategically important due to its location, offering views across large parts of the region. The ridge is a contested area in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah and has been the focus of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon in recent months.

For years, the area has been important operationally and as a sphere of influence for Hezbollah, making it a recurring flashpoint in the conflict with Israel.

The Israeli army added that soldiers would continue to operate in the security zone in southern Lebanon in order to destroy terrorist infrastructure in the area.

Despite a nominal ceasefire, Israel and Hezbollah repeatedly accuse each other of violations. The Israeli military remains deployed in southern Lebanon and carries out strikes on an almost daily basis.

articles.title: In the 1880s, Adolph Sutro built a 22-acre San Francisco estate filled with hundreds of statues and opened its gardens to the public; the mansion was later demolished and the land became a park
articles.summary: US News: On a windswept bluff overlooking the Pacific in western San Francisco, a once grand estate rose from the dunes in the 1880s, its gardens dotted with h.
articles.body: On a windswept bluff overlooking the Pacific in western San Francisco, a once grand estate rose from the dunes in the 1880s, its gardens dotted with hundreds of classical statues and its mansion visible for miles around. The property belonged to Adolph Sutro, a former mayor and entrepreneur who envisioned a cultural retreat where city residents could stroll among art, gardens and ocean views. For decades, the grounds of Sutro Heights were open to the public, drawing visitors who wandered past marble figures and manicured lawns before the mansion itself was torn down and the land eventually transformed into a city park. As recounted by SF Gate, the rise and fall of Sutro’s estate reflects both the ambitions of a Gilded Age visionary and the shifting fortunes of San Francisco’s western edge.A self made man with a grand visionAdolph Sutro arrived in San Francisco in the mid 19th century, part of the wave of newcomers drawn by the Gold Rush and the city’s rapid growth. He made his fortune not in mining but in real estate, shipping and later politics, serving as mayor in the 1890s. Unlike many of his wealthy contemporaries who built private enclaves, Sutro was interested in creating attractions that ordinary residents could enjoy. He is perhaps best known for the Sutro Baths, a massive public swimming complex near Land’s End that offered affordable recreation to working class families.Sutro Heights was conceived along similar lines, though on a more intimate scale. In the 1880s, he purchased about 22 acres on a high point above the ocean, where the air was clear and the views sweeping. There he built a large Victorian mansion surrounded by terraced gardens, winding paths and an extensive collection of statues and ornamental features. The estate was meant to be both a private residence and a public amenity, a place where San Franciscans could experience art and nature without leaving the city.An estate filled with art and ornamentThe grounds of Sutro Heights were unlike anything else in San Francisco at the time. Sutro imported hundreds of statues, mostly classical and neoclassical figures, to populate the gardens. Nymphs, muses, mythological heroes and allegorical figures stood among flower beds, shrubs and trees, creating an open air museum of sorts. Fountains, urns and decorative stonework added to the sense of a carefully composed landscape, more reminiscent of European estates than the rugged California coast.The mansion itself was a statement of wealth and taste. Built in the Victorian style, it featured multiple stories, bay windows, wraparound porches and elaborate woodwork. From its upper floors and terraces, visitors could look out over the Pacific, the Golden Gate and the Marin headlands. At night, the house and gardens were lit by electric lights, a novelty in the late 19th century that added to the estate’s allure.Sutro encouraged the public to visit. On certain days, residents could walk the grounds, admire the statues and enjoy the views. For a city that was still developing its cultural institutions, Sutro Heights offered a rare combination of art, landscape and access to the ocean.The decline of the estateAfter Sutro’s death in 1898, the fate of the estate became uncertain. His heirs faced financial pressures and the challenges of maintaining such a large property. The mansion and gardens required constant upkeep, and the salty, windy environment accelerated wear on buildings and statues alike. Over time, some of the ornamental features were removed, sold or fell into disrepair.In the early 20th century, the mansion was demolished. Accounts vary on the exact timing and reasons, but the combination of maintenance costs, changing tastes and the difficulty of finding a suitable new use for such a large private house on a remote bluff all played a part. With the main building gone, the estate lost much of its original identity. Some statues remained in place for a time, but many were relocated, vandalised or disappeared altogether.For decades, the site existed in a kind of limbo. Parts of the land were used for other purposes, while other areas sat largely neglected. The grand vision of a public cultural retreat faded from everyday memory, even as traces of the estate lingered in the landscape.From private estate to public parkIn the mid 20th century, the property that had once been Sutro Heights was incorporated into the city’s park system. The land became part of the larger network of open spaces along San Francisco’s western shore, including nearby Golden Gate National Recreation Area lands and coastal parks. Paths were reconfigured, native plants were reintroduced and the area was managed primarily for recreation and natural habitat rather than as a formal garden.Today, Sutro Heights Park is a quiet, largely open space with grassy areas, walking paths and viewpoints overlooking the ocean. Most of the original statues are gone, though a few fragments and bases remain as subtle clues to the site’s past. Interpretive signs and historical markers help visitors understand what once stood there, describing the mansion, the gardens and Sutro’s broader vision for the area.For many who visit now, the park feels like a typical San Francisco hilltop green space, valued for its views, dog walking trails and proximity to the beach. Fewer know that beneath the grass and shrubs lies the history of an ambitious experiment in public culture, when a self made millionaire tried to bring the trappings of a European estate to the edge of the Pacific.Remembering Sutro’s ambitionThe story of Sutro Heights is in many ways the story of San Francisco itself in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It was a time of rapid growth, bold entrepreneurship and grandiose projects that often outlasted their creators. Sutro’s baths, his railroad ventures and his estate all reflected a belief that the city could support large scale public attractions, even on its farthest margins.Not all of these projects endured. The Sutro Baths burned and were never rebuilt as a swimming complex, eventually becoming part of the ruins that sit near Land’s End today. The mansion at Sutro Heights was torn down, its gardens dispersed. Yet the idea behind them, that ordinary residents should have access to beauty, recreation and striking natural settings, left a mark on the city’s park system and coastal planning.Visitors who stand on the bluff today and read the historical markers can imagine the scene as it once was. A Victorian mansion crowned the hill. Statues gleamed among the flowers. Electric lights twinkled at dusk, and San Franciscans strolled the paths in their Sunday best, looking out over an ocean that felt both wild and newly accessible. That world is gone, but the land remains public, open and free, just as Sutro intended.A park with a hidden pastSutro Heights Park may not have the fame of Golden Gate Park or the Presidio, but it holds a distinctive place in the city’s history. It is a reminder that some of San Francisco’s most beloved open spaces began as private ventures with public ambitions. The park’s quiet paths and ocean views carry the echo of a more ornate past, when hundreds of statues stood where native grasses now grow and when a mansion dominated a skyline that is today defined by trees and sky.For those who take the time to look, the traces are still there. A broken pedestal here, a weathered base there, a sign describing the lost gardens. Together they tell the story of a man who tried to shape the city’s edge into a place of art and leisure, and of a landscape that, even after the mansion’s demolition and the dispersal of its ornaments, continues to serve the public in the spirit he originally envisioned.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah slipped into the pyjama row stoked by NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq this week, declaring Thursday that various histori.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah slipped into the pyjama row stoked by NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq this week, declaring Thursday that various historical accounts validate his claim about Dogra-governed Kashmir being so poor that an entire rural mohalla would own a single pair of pyjamas for residents to share when they needed to travel.“Even Sir Walter Lawrence (British civil servant and author) has talked about it. Kashmiris were suppressed deeply by landlords. Tanvir is not the first to say it. There was indeed a time when Kashmiris had to collect a pyjama from the local mosque to visit the city,” Omar said. “We have now come out of such poverty. We educate our children now.”The CM’s defence of his colleague and party spokesperson came a day after BJP workers burnt effigies of the latter over his Sept 8 remark, coinciding with the death anniversary of NC founder Sheikh Abdullah.“Our elders say Kashmiris didn’t have pyjamas to wear and one pyjama was shared by an entire mohalla during Dogra rule,” Sadiq had said, crediting Sheikh Abdullah’s land reforms in the 1950s with transforming the lives of Kashmiris.BJP accused Sadiq of insulting Kashmiri women, terming the remark an attempt to “glorify Abdullah through NC propaganda at the cost of Kashmir’s dignity”.PDP also demanded an apology, with senior party functionary Naeem Akhtar saying NC’s stand betrayed its allegedly feudal views. “They convey that progress was possible because of one party and one man, irrespective of the fact that similar reforms took place in other parts of the world at the time,” he said.Sadiq refused to apologise, citing references in Lawrence’s book The Valley of Kashmir. Lawrence, who arrived in J&K in 1889, wrote that he found the people “sullen, desperate and suspicious”.“They had been taught for years that they were serfs without rights…Pages might be written by me on facts which have come under my personal observation, but it will suffice to say that the system of administration has degraded the people and taken all heart out of them,” the NC legislator quoted from the book.Gul Wani, former head of the political science department at University of Kashmir, said the references should be read “as a metaphor for conditions in an agrarian society crushed by extreme poverty and excessive landlordism”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: What happened to The Faithful Sheriff? SuperMega’s ‘RIP’ post sparks death rumor about Twitch streamer
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A death rumor involving Twitch streamer The Faithful Sheriff spread on September 9 after SuperMega posted a message on X saying the controversial crea.
articles.body: A death rumor involving Twitch streamer The Faithful Sheriff spread on September 9 after SuperMega posted a message on X saying the controversial creator was gone. The post did not give a clear source for the claim, and there was no confirmed death announcement from a reliable news outlet. In fact, The Faithful Sheriff’s online activity has raised more questions about the report. His Twitch account remains active, and public tracking sites still list him as a creator with more than 122,000 followers. The streamer has also been linked to recent activity on X.The Faithful Sheriff death rumor began after SuperMega’s X postThe confusion started when the official SuperMega account posted about The Faithful Sheriff on September 9. The sketch comedy duo wrote, “W*F, just saw The Faithful Sheriff news. Memes aside, it’s crazy to think that he’s gone. He was definitely controversial, but no one deserves to go out in the way he did... RIP.” The post was enough to make people question whether the streamer had actually died.There was a major problem with treating that message as confirmation: no reliable death report appeared to support it. A death claim about a public creator needs more than a social media post, especially when the post itself does not explain where the information came from.The Faithful Sheriff’s public accounts also point to an active creator. TwitchMetrics currently lists 122,129 followers on his Twitch channel and says he streamed for 95 hours during the previous 30 days, with an average of 98 viewers in that period. Streams Charts gives a similar figure, listing about 122,000 followers and a 95-viewer average over 30 days.The streamer has also remained active around gaming and sports discussions. A post attributed to his X account after the SuperMega message discussed the Patriots-Seahawks game and said, “What a CRAZY ending to that Patriots vs Seahawks game.” That recent activity is another reason the death claim should not be treated as confirmed.The Faithful Sheriff and TheBurntPeanut had already been involved in online dramaThe Faithful Sheriff is known for using a peanut-style character dressed as a sheriff while mixing gaming content with Christian messages. His own website describes him as a streamer and content creator focused on “Bringing the Gospel to Gamers.” He became known under the name DrWitnesser before taking the Faithful Sheriff name and using the peanut character.His connection to TheBurntPeanut became another part of his online story. In April 2026, The Faithful Sheriff publicly questioned why he had been banned from TheBurntPeanut’s Discord server. He also said his name was blocked in TheBurntPeanut’s Twitch chat, meaning messages containing his name would not appear.The Faithful Sheriff later explained the issue again, saying, “The mods actually blocked my name. The Faithful Sheriff is blocked in his stream. You cannot say The Faithful Sheriff in the stream; therefore, my name. Like anything I say is blocked.”That earlier dispute is relevant because The Faithful Sheriff and TheBurntPeanut use similar peanut-based streamer characters, but they are separate creators. The Faithful Sheriff’s rebrand and the dispute with TheBurntPeanut were already drawing attention months before the latest death rumor.For now, there is no reliable confirmation that The Faithful Sheriff has died. The SuperMega post started the claim, but available public activity does not support treating the death as established fact. Until a verified statement comes from the streamer, his representatives, family or another reliable source, the report remains an unconfirmed rumor.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Need social media firewalls, safeguards for minors: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: With minors' access to social media platforms banned in many countries, Supreme Court Thursday took the first step in this regard by seekin.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With minors' access to social media platforms banned in many countries, Supreme Court Thursday took the first step in this regard by seeking govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract - which is impermissible for a person below 18 years of age under Indian law.The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka, on behalf of NGO Just Rights for Children Association, found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which said there was a need for safeguards and firewalls to protect minors.Phoolka said children were at present permitted to independently create and maintain accounts on social media platforms and access digital platforms "notwithstanding their statutory incapacity to enter into a contract under Section 11 of Indian Contract Act, 1872", and said such contracts are void ab initio.The NGO said the absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposed children to "foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content and other harms affecting their safety, dignity, development and well-being".It requested the court to direct govt to ensure that persons below 18 years of age are not permitted to enter into contracts with digital platforms, including social media, online gaming, content-sharing, live-streaming and other user generated content platforms. It said minors could be permitted to access lawful, educational and age-appropriate digital content through accounts maintained and controlled by their parents or guardians, subject to an appropriate regulatory framework.Phoolka said social media platforms applied US law in India, not Indian law. In US, a person above 13 years can lawfully enter into a contract. CJI Kant said, "We need some safeguards in India." Justice Bagchi said, "There should be some firewalls."The NGO said opening of accounts includes acceptance of contractual terms and conditions, user agreements, privacy policy, etc, which govern the relationship between the platform and the user.Referring to provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the NGO said Section 9 required verifiable parental or guardian consent for processing a child's personal data. The Act also imposes restrictions concerning detrimental processing, tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising, it said.However, the existing statutory framework does not expressly prohibit a person below 18 from independently creating an account on a digital platform nor does it prescribe a uniform mechanism for preventing such independent opening of accounts, it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Last day of work is last day in US: Immigration expert suggests 6 steps if 60-day grace period for H-1B ends
articles.summary: US News: As the Donald Trump administration Thursday moved towards ending the 60-day grace period for several work visa holders, panic spread as the H-1B visa .
articles.body: As the Donald Trump administration Thursday moved towards ending the 60-day grace period for several work visa holders, panic spread as the H-1B visa is one of them and the proposal would mean that an H-1B holder will have to leave the US immediately if they lose their jobs.Under current immigration laws, holders of certain visas, particularly H-1B visas, which are non-immigrant visas that allow employers to sponsor skilled workers with Bachelor's degrees or higher, get a 60-day grace period to find a new job if they lose the employment tied to their visa. "This proposal restores a direct relationship between an alien’s nonimmigrant status and the specific employment or activity that formed the basis of his or her admission or grant of status in the United States and reduces administrative burden," the proposal said.Immigration lawyer Sonal Sharma cautioned that it is still a proposal and can be rejected, modified, or implemented as is."This is only a proposal. The 60-day grace period is still in effect right now. Don’t make any decisions based just on this proposal, and be careful about online claims that the grace period is already gone. The final rule could be adopted as is, changed, delayed, or even withdrawn. Its start date and any transition rules will be set if and when a final rule is issued," Sharma wrote in a LinkedIn post.6 things to do if this rule takes effect exactly as the proposalConsider your last day of work as your last day of visa status. Make sure you have a plan to leave or transition before your job ends, not after.Submit any change-of-employer, change-of-status, or extension applications early, ideally before your job ends, since there won’t be time to stay and look for new work.Think about using premium processing or portability options (like H-1B AC21 portability) to make sure a new petition is filed before your current job ends.Employers should plan for immigration timing when offboarding employees, and remember that H-1B and O-1 sponsors may need to cover reasonable return travel costs.Keep in mind that leaving and reentering the US can be a backup plan, since a new approved petition usually allows you to come back.Keep an eye on the Federal Register and the official docket for updates on the final rule and when it will take effect.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Morocco denies involvement in migrant surge into Spain’s Ceuta
articles.summary: Over 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta, sparking a humanitarian crisis and political tensions between Spain and Morocco.
articles.body:
Morocco’s Foreign Ministry says there is no evidence of Rabat’s involvement in the mass migrant crossing into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta in July.

More than 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta from nearby Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented surge that left scores dead and sparked European Union infighting over migration.

While most have ⁠since returned, more than 100 people died , according to local officials and civil organisations.

Local authorities say thousands – including unaccompanied minors – remain in the enclave where they are living in makeshift camps or on the streets and beaches. Their presence has fuelled near-daily protests by residents angry at the Spanish ‌government’s handling of the crisis.

Spain’s opposition parties have since targeted the government’s relationship with Morocco and accused Rabat of facilitating or orchestrating the crossing.

“Why continue to level accusations against Morocco when no evidence, facts, or reports establish any involvement on the part of Moroccan authorities?” the ministry said in a statement on Thursday.

“Why are illegal migrants ⁠not being returned, even though the Moroccan government has ⁠officially committed to readmitting them? Why are unaccompanied minors being kept away from their families, when Morocco has urgently requested their return?” it added.

The ministry asserted that Morocco refuses to ⁠be used as a “pre-election political pawn”, nor does it accept being made the “scapegoat in political score-settling”. Spain will hold national elections by mid-2027.

The Moroccan Foreign Ministry highlighted the close security, migration and economic ties between Rabat and Madrid since Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez backed Morocco’s autonomy plan for Western Sahara in 2022.

On Wednesday, Spain declassified intelligence reports that had warned of potential “mass entries” by migrants into Ceuta just before the incident occurred.

A declassified military intelligence document from July 30 stated that it is “highly likely that the Moroccan authorities are not actively encouraging the migratory wave, but have so far acted in a negligent and passive manner”.

Morocco ‌does ‌not recognise Spanish sovereignty over Ceuta or Melilla, the other autonomous Spanish enclave bordering Morocco.
